panels.description: One row per server in the cluster. "Load" is how busy that server's VoltDB process is: the percentage of CPU it is using (0-100%) - this is the Volt process only, not the whole machine. The row also shows how long the server has been up, its software version, and whether cross-datacenter replication (XDCR) is ready on it.
panels.title: Nodes

panels.description: The number of milliseconds difference between the system clock time of the current host and the remote host.
panels.title: Clock skew

panels.description: The total number of connections that were rejected because the connection limit had been reached.
panels.title: Dropped

panels.description:
- `voltdb_client_connections_limit_total`: The maximum number of client connections allowed for the server.
- `voltdb_accepted_connections_total`: The total number of client connections opened since the server started, including connections that are now closed.
panels.title: Free conns

panels.description:
- `voltdb_file_descriptors_limit_total`: The maximum number of file descriptors allowed for the process running the server.
- `voltdb_file_descriptors_count_total`: The number of file descriptors open in the process.
panels.title: FD usage

panels.description: The maximum number of file descriptors allowed for the process running the server.
panels.title: FD limit

panels.description: Cumulative run time of garbage collection. Tags: GC_TYPE - (e.g. CMS, G1), example gc_type="G1 Young Generation".
panels.title: GC

panels.description: Reports the status of recent rebalancing operations. Informational metric. Tags: BALANCE_MOVED_ROWS - The number of rows of data that have been moved. BALANCE_PERCENTAGE_MOVED - The percentage of the total segments that have already been moved. BALANCE_ROWS_PER_SECOND - The average number of rows moved per second. BALANCE_ESTIMATED_REMAINING - The estimated time remaining until the rebalance is complete. BALANCE_MEGABYTES_PER_SECOND - The average volume of data moved per second, measured in megabytes. BALANCE_CALLS_PER_SECOND - The average number of rebalance work units, or transactions, executed per second. BALANCE_CALLS_LATENCY - The average total time between start and finish of rebalance operations. (TODO: in millis? should be in seconds) BALANCE_CALLS_TIME - The average execution time for rebalance transactions. (TODO: in millis? should be in seconds) BALANCE_CALLS_TRANSFER_TIME - The average time spent transferring data during rebalance transactions. (TODO: in millis? should be in seconds)
panels.title: Rebalance

panels.description: Number of transactions executed by the connected clients
panels.title: Transactions/s

panels.description: The number of procedure invocation per 5 minutes, also includes procedures being replicated into partition replicas, so it does not equal the number of transactions issued by clients
panels.title: Procedure calls

panels.description:
- `voltdb_procedure_aborted_total`: The number of times the procedure was aborted.
- `voltdb_procedure_failed_total`: The number of times the procedure failed unexpectedly.
panels.title: Procedure errors

panels.description: The distribution of length of time it took to execute the stored procedure.
panels.title: Max Latency

panels.description: The number of import transactions that succeeded.
panels.title: Import TPS

panels.description: The number of transactions that have been initiated for which the log has yet to be written to disk. For synchronous logging, this value is always zero.
panels.title: Commandlog queue

panels.description: The number of times the stored procedure has been invoked by this connection on this host node.
panels.title: Transaction rate

panels.description: The distribution of length of time it took to execute the stored procedure.
panels.title: 999th percentile request execution time (whole transaction path)

panels.description: The length of time it took to execute the stored procedure.
panels.title: Max procedure execution time (just the procedure)

panels.description: The busiest server's CPU usage right now - the highest VoltDB CPU percentage across all servers. A high value here points to a single overloaded node even when the rest of the cluster is fine.
panels.title: Max CPU Usage

panels.description: The most memory-stressed server in the cluster: the largest share of a server's memory being used by VoltDB, as a percentage. It shows the single busiest server (not a cluster average) so one hot node isn't hidden. Use the Memory dashboard for a per-server breakdown.
panels.title: Worst RAM usage

panels.description: The server closest to its Java memory limit: the largest share of the available Java heap in use across all servers, as a percentage. Values near 100% risk pauses or out-of-memory errors. Use the Memory dashboard for per-server detail.
panels.title: Worst heap usage

panels.description: The percentage of CPU used by the database server process. 0-100.
panels.title: CPU Usage

panels.description: The resident set size. That is, the total amount of memory allocated to the VoltDB processes on the server.
panels.title: RSS size

panels.description: The amount of memory allocated by Java and in use by VoltDB.
panels.title: Java Heap Memory Usage

panels.description:
- `voltdb_client_connections_limit_total`: The maximum number of client connections allowed for the server.
- `voltdb_client_connections_open_total`: The number of client connections open on the server.

panels.description: The number of file descriptors open in the process.

panels.description: The number of individual messages sent from the client to the host.

panels.description: How often command logging fell so far behind that it had to pause transactions. Any value above zero means writes to the command log couldn't keep up, usually because the disk holding it is slow or saturated. Applies only when command logging runs in asynchronous mode.
panels.title: Command log backpressure

panels.description: When command logging last had to pause transactions to catch up. Shows a placeholder if it never has.
panels.title: Last backpressure

panels.description: How long it takes to create a new command-log file on disk (99th percentile). Rising times point to a slow or busy disk holding the command log.
panels.title: Command log segment allocation time (p99)
